clues: This city sits on the coast in south Europe, right by the sea. A high rocky hill stands at its heart.
Summers turn fierce here, in part since the built up streets trap heat. The packed city makes its own hot air and holds it close.
In 1834 this small town was picked as the new capital of a free land. Leaders chose it for its grand past and deep meaning.
A grand stone temple crowns the steep rock at the heart of this town. It was built in a golden age when free votes first shaped the land.
The parliament of Greece makes its laws in this city. Its members meet in a grand old palace built for a king.
